title: Jurel's Unbeaten 99 Rescues India A After Collapse Against New Zealand A
excerpt: Captain Dhruv Jurel was 99 not out at stumps as India A reached 291 for 7 on Day 1 of the second unofficial Test in Christchurch, after Devdutt Padikkal's 80 and a collapse to 160 for 6.
body:
• India A closed Day 1 of the second unofficial Test against New Zealand A on 291 for 7 in 88 overs at Hagley Oval, Christchurch.
  • Captain Dhruv Jurel was unbeaten on 99 from 155 balls, with 11 fours and three sixes, after India A slipped to 160 for 6.
  • Devdutt Padikkal made 80 and shared a 91-run second-wicket stand with Sai Sudharsan, who made 41.
  • Fraser Sheat took 4 for 50 for New Zealand A; Jurel will resume on Day 2 one run short of a century, with Akash Deep unbeaten on 25.

Dhruv Jurel finished Day 1 unbeaten on 99 as India A recovered to 291 for 7 against New Zealand A in the second unofficial Test at Hagley Oval, Christchurch, on October 31. India A had slipped to 160 for 6 after a middle-order collapse, before Jurel rebuilt the innings with the lower order, according to ESPNcricinfo.

Early wicket, then Padikkal and Sudharsan rebuild

India A lost Yashasvi Jaiswal for a four-ball duck in the opening over, lbw to Fraser Sheat. Sai Sudharsan, promoted to open, and Devdutt Padikkal then batted through the remainder of the first session and added 91 runs for the second wicket.

https://x.com/ImTanujSingh/status/2116403378884690229

Sudharsan made 41 off 63 balls before he was dismissed by Jarrod McKay shortly after lunch. Yash Rathod made 13 before edging Brett Randell, leaving India A at 131 for 3, according to the IANS report carried by NewKerala.

Padikkal, who had scored 199 in the first unofficial Test last week, made 80 with 12 boundaries. ESPNcricinfo reported that he batted outside his crease to counter late movement and brought up his half-century in the second session. His dismissal, bowled by Sheat, started the collapse.

Three wickets for six runs

ESPNcricinfo reported that India A lost 3 for 6 in six deliveries in the afternoon session. Padikkal chopped on, R. Smaran was lbw first ball, and Washington Sundar was also dismissed as Sheat's late inswing accounted for wickets that were either lbw or bowled. The IANS report put the slide at 137 for 3 to 137 for 5, and then to 160 for 6.

Sheat finished the day with 4 for 50. Randell, McKay and left-arm spinner Jayden Lennox took one wicket each, according to IANS.

Jurel marshals the lower order

At 160 for 6, Jurel set about rebuilding. He added 62 runs for the seventh wicket with Manav Suthar, who made 22 before driving Lennox and nicking behind, ESPNcricinfo reported. Jurel then added an unbroken 69 runs with Akash Deep, who was unbeaten on 25 at stumps.

Jurel reached the 90s in the 79th over and played out the remaining overs to close on 99 not out from 155 balls, with 11 fours and three sixes. It was a return to run-scoring after scores of 1 and 2 in last week's first unofficial Test, ESPNcricinfo said.

What it means and what's next

The match is not complete, so there is no result to report. India A's Day 1 total gives their bowlers a larger cushion than looked likely at 160 for 6, in ESPNcricinfo's assessment. Play resumes on Day 2 of the fixture scheduled from October 31 to November 3 at Christchurch, with Jurel one run short of a century and Akash Deep alongside him. New Zealand A have not yet batted.
